_comment: NEXPIRE Model A — Category Shelf-Life Baseline Lookup Table
_note: This is the single source of truth for urgency normalization. Edit here to add categories.

_urgency_curve_types.linear_convex: Used for short-shelf perishables. Urgency rises roughly linearly from day 0, with a slight convex acceleration in the final 20% of shelf life.
_urgency_curve_types.sigmoid: Used for long-shelf items (pantry, perfume, frozen). Stays near-0 until the final ~10% of shelf life, then rises sharply. Parameters: steepness k, inflection point (fraction of shelf life).

Dairy.description: Milk, yogurt, paneer, butter, cheese. Near-zero tolerance for delay. Spoilage risk compounds daily in warm conditions.

Bakery.description: Bread, buns, cakes, pastries. Very fast decay, often stale before unsafe.

Fruits & Veggies.description: Fresh produce. High weather sensitivity — heat accelerates decay, monsoon can reduce demand for certain items.

Meat & Seafood.description: Fresh meat, poultry, fish, shellfish. Fastest decay and highest food-safety risk. Markdown ceiling is aggressive.

Ready-to-Eat.description: Prepared meals, meal kits, hot counter items. Very short window, similar dynamics to Bakery.

Beverages.description: Packaged juices, dairy drinks, carbonated. Moderate shelf life. Weather affects demand (hot weather boosts cold drink sales).

Snacks.description: Chips, biscuits, namkeen. Moderate shelf life. Low weather sensitivity.

Food Grains.description: Rice, atta, dal, pulses. Long shelf life. Urgency near-zero until final 7% of shelf life. Very low weather sensitivity.

Oil & Masala.description: Cooking oils, masalas, condiments. Long shelf, near-irrelevant urgency until close to expiry. Tiny weather sensitivity.

Frozen.description: Frozen vegetables, ice cream, frozen meals. Moderate shelf. Cold-chain dependent.

Perfume & Cosmetics.description: Perfumes, lotions, cosmetics. Urgency is near-irrelevant until well under 5% of shelf life remains (~45 days for a 2-yr product). Zero weather sensitivity.
